title: FeelAnyForce released tactile/depth split files (TacForce)
rights: CC BY 4.0 per the pinned Hugging Face dataset card. Credit the paper authors and dataset uploader amirsh1376. Only new aggregate statistics, sample identities, file digests and independent readers are included.

related_paper_keys: FeelAnyForce: Estimating Contact Force Feedback from Tactile Sensation for Vision-Based Tactile Sensors
history.interpretation: Associated paper already screened. The pinned data release and exact split files are checked separately.

queries_and_followup: Followed FeelAnyForce project and code dataset links to the Hugging Face tree; checked tactile/depth/FT paths in the three label files, then compared the meaning of the default test split with the paper methods and source code.
evidence: All labels and the ZIP64 central directory inspected. Exactly one complete PNG + depth NPY pair from each of the seven membership combinations inspected, with CRC32, SHA-256 and dimensions. Other members were verified at directory-entry level.
interpretation: The release has six numeric components per label. dataset.py selects the first three. The test CSV is configured as labels_test_seen in args.py and used for the seen evaluation in training_multi_head.py. The study separately evaluates unseen indenters.

2,106/2,864 distinct test paths also occur with identical tactile/depth paths and identical six-number targets in training or validation (1,921 + 225 − 40). Seven membership counts appear in feel-payload-checks.csv, once for each modality. The remaining 758 test paths are unique to that split by pathname. This result concerns only the released seen split.

Authors describe taring before each contact during capture and the inability to do so over the entire pushing interval in their real-world experiment, author PDF p. 6. No standalone absolute moment reference follows from the six published labels.
reproduction: Save the tree API response as tree.json, place all three TacForce CSVs beside it, and run python derive_feel.py ROOT OUT --fetch (Python and NumPy). It retrieves the end records, central directory and example payloads using validated HTTP 206 ranges from the pinned four-volume ZIP. Later runs can use the local cache.
